topic: Phonics with s, i, t, p, n: common letter sounds and short-i words made only from those letters

objectives.question: What sound does each letter—s, i, t, p, n—make?
objectives.text: Identify and produce the primary sound for each letter in the set (s, i, t, p, n), distinguishing the short vowel /ɪ/ from the consonant sounds.
objectives.connection: Learners must know the individual phoneme associated with each grapheme before blending them into words.
evidenceCriteria: Identifies the correct grapheme when given its sound /s/, /t/, /p/, /n/, or /ɪ/
Produces the target continuant sound (/s/, /n/, /ɪ/) when presented with the letterform

objectives.question: How do individual sounds blend together into short-i words like sit, pin, and tip?
objectives.text: Blend sequential phonemes made from {s, i, t, p, n} to decode short-i VC and CVC words orally.
objectives.connection: Combines mastery of isolated letter sounds into continuous auditory and visual word decoding.
evidenceCriteria: Blends spoken phonemes /s/ /ɪ/ /t/ to say 'sit'
Reads aloud CVC target words (e.g., 'pin', 'tip', 'tin') composed exclusively of the taught letters

objectives.question: How do we segment a spoken word and choose the matching letters to spell it?
objectives.text: Segment spoken short-i words (e.g., sip, pit, nip) into constituent phonemes and map each sound to its corresponding letter in order.
objectives.connection: Deepens decoding into bidirectional sound-symbol correspondence through encoding (spelling).
evidenceCriteria: Identifies the medial short vowel /ɪ/ in a spoken CVC word from the target set
Places the correct letters into Elkonin boxes to encode spoken words using s, i, t, p, n

validation.note: Checks references and declarations only; human review and hydrated lesson QA must establish quality and actual coverage.

gaps.reason: The see_hear eval mode of letter-sound-link only supports continuants (/s/, /n/) and short vowels (/ɪ/); stop consonants (/t/, /p/) cannot be assessed via unaided isolated oral production by five-year-olds due to acoustic coarticulation limitations.
Cold reading of printed CVC words without auditory support is deferred because kindergarten non-readers require auditory blending support before cold visual decoding.

topic: Phonics with s, i, t, p, n: common letter sounds and short-i words made only from those letters

objectives.question: What sound does each letter in the group s, i, t, p, n make?

objectives.question: How do we count objects without skipping any or counting the same one twice?
objectives.text: Apply one-to-one correspondence by tagging or touching each object in a collection of up to 10 items exactly once while reciting the number sequence in order.
objectives.connection: Establishes the fundamental physical and verbal coordination needed before the learner can determine total set size.
evidenceCriteria: Learner touches or taps each visual object in sequence without skipping or double-counting.
Learner matches each physical touch to a consecutive number word from 1 up to 10.

objectives.question: What does the last number we say tell us about the group?
objectives.text: Identify that the final number spoken when counting represents the total quantity (cardinality) of the group of up to 10 objects.
objectives.connection: Builds directly on one-to-one correspondence by shifting focus from the act of counting to understanding the total quantity.
evidenceCriteria: When asked 'How many are there?', learner states the final counted number without recounting from one.
Learner correctly identifies the total quantity of scattered or lined groups up to 10.

objectives.question: Which written number shows how many things we counted?
objectives.text: Match a counted quantity of 1 to 10 objects to its corresponding written numeral.
objectives.connection: Connects concrete quantities and spoken cardinal counts to standard symbolic numeral representations.
evidenceCriteria: Given a counted set of objects (1-10), learner selects or names the matching written numeral.

gaps.reason: Closing independent assessment evaluates cardinality and numeral matching via tap selection; unassisted physical one-to-one touch tagging without interface scaffolding is not captured in the closing evaluation.
